scispace_question: How is radiative recombination of nonthermal electrons with hydrogenic He III ions represented by an energy dependent cross section and emitted photon energy, and how can electron kinetic, atomic binding, and retained radiation energy be conserved in kinetic plasma models?

sources.title: The electron energy loss rate due to radiative recombination
sources.authors: Junjie Mao, Jelle Kaastra, N. R. Badnell
sources.read_scope: Primary full-text extraction through section3; equations1-6 and sections1,2.1,2.2 inspected.
sources.supports: Milne detailed-balance relation for level-resolved RR; distinct count and kinetic-energy moments of a cross section; Maxwellian-averaged thermal coefficients require a specified distribution.
sources.limits: These Maxwellian coefficients do not qualify a physical rate or mean spectrum for our stored nonthermal integrated returns. Our diagnostic mapping follows exact provider source rather than reusing a thermal rate.
sources.summary: The paper computes recombination rate and electron kinetic-loss coefficients as different velocity moments, using cross sections obtained from photoionization through detailed balance. It explicitly adopts a Maxwellian distribution for its thermal-rate calculation.

sources.read_scope: SciSpace bibliographic/abstract and Exa abstract/reference extraction only; full derivation not retrieved.

sources.limits: Not used as equation-level evidence or new provider calibration. Search duplicate repository dates2022 were not treated as new publication dates.

wolfram_context_status: Automated context supplied generic photon energy and thermal-energy snippets, plus no-result messages. None of the generic thermal equations was adopted as this research's caloric law.
new_claim: Conservative integrated diagnostic lift and exact normalization/interface JVP, based on fixed provider moments. No strong no-go or novelty priority claim.
